After subtracting the common energy, the reduced matrix has only two couplings and satisfies \(M^3=\Omega^2M\) with \(\Omega^2=(32(n-2)+\delta^2)/4\). The closed exponential gives a single-cosine transfer amplitude, so the displayed times are global maximizers and all corollaries follow algebraically. A fresh independent matrix replay checked the cubic identity and exact maximum for representative \(n,\delta\); the frozen verifier additionally compares an independent power-series exponential, target boundaries and asymptotics.

final_claim: For the single-excitation \(XY\) Hamiltonian on \(K_n\) with the input-output edge deleted, hopping two, and endpoint shifts \(2n-6\pm\delta/2\), the exact maximum transfer fidelity is \(\left(32(n-2)/(32(n-2)+\delta^2)\right)^2\), attained at the stated odd half-periods; this gives the exact target-fidelity window, fixed-error asymptotic, and nontrivial \(\delta=c\sqrt n\) limit.
